about: The session list as the web console groups it (byMachine and listView in ui/src/model/session.ts), the reference for both phones: docs/session-liveness.md, 'Client presentation policy'; SE-C17 to SE-C19, SE-C23, SE-C24, SE-C29, SE-C32, SE-C33, SE-C43, SE-C219, SE-C220 and SE-C222 in docs/web-console-contracts.md. A hosted router's sessions from more than one machine are headed per machine as the phones head them (SessionGroups.byMachine), as decided on 2026-10-05.

Read by ui/src/model/shared-fixtures.spec.ts, ios/AgentRouter/Tests/SharedFixtureTests.swift and android/app/src/test/java/ca/whnet/agentrouter/SharedFixtureTest.kt. Each groups `sessions` as its own client does, maps the result to the shape below and compares it with `expected`.

`expected` is generated from the web's model, never written by hand: edit a case's name, now, sessions or pending, then in ui/ run `UPDATE_SHARED_FIXTURES=1 pnpm exec vitest run src/model/shared-fixtures.spec.ts`.

`pending` marks a case the clients disagree on where a phone would lose information by matching the web. Every suite skips it, by name, until it is decided; `expected` still records what the web does.

`now` is the device's clock, in epoch milliseconds. `sessions` are rows as GET /api/live/sessions returns them; their `as_of_ms` is the router's clock, here seven minutes behind the device's unless a case says otherwise.

`expected` is one of two shapes. A list with no machine heading, which is a local router's and a hosted router's with one machine or none named, is {recent, older, archived}. A hosted router's list from more than one machine is {machines}: its parts in the order they are headed, each {machine, recent, older, archived}, where machine is the label the router gives the machine (machine.label, trimmed; a blank one names no machine) and recent, older and archived are what that machine's sessions alone make. Machines are in alphabetical order, case aside. Rows that name no machine, beside machines that do, come last, in a part whose machine is null, which every client heads 'Unnamed machine'.

expected.recent: the projects in the order they are listed, each {project, tone, halo, sessions}. project is the heading's name; sessions are the ids in the order listed; tone is the heading dot's tone as the client ranks it, one of busy, attention, warn, error, idle and closed (the hollow ring), or null for the plain neutral dot; halo is whether that dot wears the halo of a live session. How a tone is drawn is each client's own: the phones draw a neutral dot gray, and Android draws no dot at all for an idle project from an older router (SE-C19).
expected.older: the projects folded under 'older', in the same shape. expected.archived: the shelf's session ids, in order.

cases.name: projects are in alphabetical order, case aside, and sessions newest first within each (SE-C24)
a session quiet for more than twelve hours folds into older, grouped by project, and a live one never does (SE-C29)
twelve hours quiet is still recent, and a moment more is older (SE-C29)
the twelve hours are measured on the router's clock, here eight days behind this device's (SE-C43)
the twelve hours are measured on the router's clock, here a day ahead of this device's (SE-C43)
the shelf holds exactly what the router marks archived, flat and newest first, however recently it moved (SE-C32, SE-C33)
a project's dot is its most pressing session: waiting over failed over stalled over working over idle, and the hollow ring only once every session has ended (SE-C18)
an activity this screen does not know outranks nothing and has not ended, and a tone it does not know defers to the activity (SE-C2, SE-C3, SE-C18)
a project is the last segment of the cwd, a Windows path's included, else the router's own name for it (SE-C23)
two projects whose names differ only in case stay two projects, lowercase first (SE-C24)
names sort as the web sorts them: punctuation before digits before letters, _ before - before . (SE-C24)
a list from an older router, which names no activity: a heading is busy while anything in it is active, else idle, and the fold goes by this device's clock (SE-C17, SE-C19)
a hosted router's rows from one machine list exactly as a local router's
rows from several machines are headed per machine, alphabetically and case aside, each machine with its own projects, its own older fold and its own shelf (SE-C219, SE-C220)
a machine with nothing recent still has its part, holding only its older fold or only its shelf, and a Windows machine's project is the last segment of its cwd (SE-C219, SE-C220, SE-C222)
rows that name no machine, beside machines that do, come last in a part of their own, and a label is read trimmed (SE-C220)
one machine's rows beside rows that name none are one list with no heading, as one machine's alone are (SE-C219)
an empty list has no projects, no older fold and no shelf
